faq.a: Latitude tells you how far north or south of the Equator a place is, measured in degrees. The Equator is 0 degrees and the poles are 90 degrees north and south.
The Equator is the imaginary line around the middle of the Earth, at 0 degrees latitude. It splits the world into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
asks: Which countries are on the Equator?

faq.a: The Tropic of Cancer, at 23.5 degrees north, and the Tropic of Capricorn, at 23.5 degrees south, mark how far from the Equator the midday sun can be straight overhead. The warm belt between them is called the tropics.
asks: What is the Tropic of Cancer?

faq.q: What happens at the Arctic Circle?
faq.a: North of the Arctic Circle there is at least one summer day with 24 hours of daylight and at least one winter day with no sunrise at all. The Antarctic Circle does the same in the south.
asks: Why does the sun not set in the Arctic summer?

faq.q: Why is it hotter near the Equator?
faq.a: Near the Equator the sun shines from high overhead, so its energy hits the ground straight on and is concentrated. Near the poles sunlight comes in at a low slant and is spread over a bigger area.

facts: The Equator is about 40,075 km long.
The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight states of India.

quiz.say: What is the latitude of the Equator?
quiz.why: The Equator is the starting line for latitude, so it is 0 degrees.

wrong.1: 90 degrees is the latitude of the North and South Poles.
wrong.2: 23.5 degrees north is the Tropic of Cancer.

quiz.say: Which line passes through Kenya, Brazil and Indonesia?
quiz.show: Kenya, Brazil and Indonesia all sit on…
quiz.why: The Equator crosses all three countries.

wrong.1: The Arctic Circle is far north, through Norway, Russia and Canada.
wrong.2: The Tropic of Capricorn crosses Brazil, but not Kenya or Indonesia.
